summary: ITU-T G.709 introduced new ODU containers (ODU0, ODU4, ODU2e, and ODUflex) and more flexibility. This document updates the ODU-related parts of RFC 4328 with GMPLS signaling extensions to control the full set of OTN features.

plainLanguage.summary: Optical Transport Networks carry client signals inside ODU containers. RFC 7139 extends GMPLS signaling so routers can request the newer container types, reserve their tributary slots and resize certain ODUflex connections.

how many tributary slots does oduflex need
subtitle: GMPLS signaling for the newer ODU containers and tributary-slot arrangements in G.709 optical networks.

tldr.problem: The earlier GMPLS signaling covered an older G.709 revision and could not describe newer ODU containers, slot sizes and multiplexing options.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7139 extends RSVP-TE traffic parameters and defines an OTN-TDM generalized label with a Tributary Port Number and a bit map of reserved slots; it also defines resizing procedures for ODUflex(GFP).
tldr.outcome: The RFC updates the ODU-related parts of RFC 4328 and was updated by RFC 7892.

today: RFC 7139 is a Proposed Standard published in March 2014. It updates RFC 4328 and has been updated by RFC 7892.

sections.title: Why G.709 Signaling Was Extended
sections.content:
The 2012 revision of ITU-T G.709 added ODU0, ODU2e, ODU4 and ODUflex containers, along with a 1.25 Gbps tributary-slot granularity. Earlier GMPLS signaling in RFC 4328 covered a previous G.709 revision and did not signal all these newer types and multiplexing features.

RFC 7139 updates the ODU-related signaling using Resource Reservation Protocol - Traffic Engineering (RSVP-TE). It extends traffic parameters and defines a flexible OTN-TDM Generalized Label that carries tributary-slot and port information.
sections.plainLanguage: G.709 added new optical containers and ways to divide them into slots. This RFC adds signaling fields that let routers request and describe those resources.

sections.title: Traffic Parameters for ODU Signals
sections.content:
OTN-TDM traffic parameters travel in the SENDER_TSPEC object in a Path message and the FLOWSPEC object in a Resv message. They identify a Signal Type, the number of virtual components, a multiplier and a bit rate. New Signal Types cover ODU4, OCh at 100 Gbps, ODU0, ODU2e and ODUflex forms.

For ODUflex, the Bit_Rate field carries the nominal rate as a 32-bit IEEE single-precision floating-point number. ODUflex requires NVC to be 0 and MT to be 1. For other Signal Types, Bit_Rate must be zero when sent. Nodes check that the requested type and rate are supported and report an RSVP error if not.
sections.plainLanguage: The signaling request names the optical signal and its required rate. Each node checks whether it can support that request before reserving network resources.

sections.title: Allocating Slots for ODUflex(CBR)
sections.content:
For ODUflex with a constant bit rate, each higher-order ODU link must reserve enough tributary slots for the requested rate and the specified tolerances. The number of slots is rounded up from the ODUflex rate divided by the usable rate of one slot on that link.

Because tributary-slot rates differ among higher-order ODU links, the same connection may use different slot counts along its route. In the RFC's example, a 2.5 Gbps service reserves 2 slots on an ODU4 link and 3 slots on an ODU2 link.
sections.plainLanguage: Each optical link calculates how many of its slots a connection needs. The same ODUflex connection can need a different number of slots on different link types.

sections.title: The OTN-TDM Generalized Label
sections.content:
The OTN-TDM Generalized Label describes how a lower-order ODU is placed into a higher-order ODU. Its fixed part contains a 12-bit Tributary Port Number (TPN), a reserved byte and a 12-bit Length. A variable bit map follows, with optional zero padding to make the full label a multiple of four bytes.

The TPN identifies the tributary port used for demultiplexing. The Length says how many slot bits are in the map, and each map bit marks a slot as used or unused. For a direct ODU-to-OTU mapping, the TPN and Length are zero and no bit map is included.
sections.plainLanguage: The label tells the receiving node which tributary port identifies the signal and which slots carry it. A bit map marks the slots reserved for that signal.

sections.title: Assigning and Checking Labels
sections.content:
The ingress node requests the OTN-TDM switching type and the matching payload identifier. A downstream node selects available slots, assigns a valid TPN that does not conflict with other connections, and returns the label. The upstream node reads the slot map and places the TPN in the optical overhead so the receiving node can check it.

A node rejects a label that violates local policy, gives an invalid length or TPN, requests unsupported slot granularity, or marks a number of slots inconsistent with the traffic parameters. The node reports an unacceptable-label error to the neighboring signaling node.
sections.plainLanguage: The downstream node chooses available slots and returns a label describing that choice. The upstream node checks the label and signals an error if the values conflict with the request or local rules.

sections.title: Resizing ODUflex(GFP) Connections
sections.content:
For hitless adjustment of ODUflex(GFP), the control plane must start the adjustment using the Shared Explicit reservation style. To increase bandwidth, the ingress sends a new Path message with the same Tunnel ID and a new LSP ID. Downstream nodes reserve additional slots and return both the old and new labels; after successful adjustment, the ingress should remove the old control state.

For a decrease, the ingress should also use a Shared Explicit Path message. Once the data-plane resize completes, it should send a ResvErr to remove the old control state.
sections.plainLanguage: To change capacity, the control plane first signals a replacement reservation while the old one is still present. Once the resize succeeds, it removes the old state.

sections.title: Security and IANA Assignments
sections.content:
RFC 7139 changes information carried in existing GMPLS signaling and says it introduces no new security considerations. It points to the security measures in RFC 3473 and RFC 4328 and the GMPLS security overview in RFC 5920.

IANA assigned the OTN-TDM object type for the RSVP-TE traffic parameters, updated Generalized PID values and created an OTN Signal Type subregistry. New Signal Type assignments require Standards Action.
sections.plainLanguage: The new signaling fields use the existing GMPLS security model. IANA records the signal and payload numbers so implementations can interpret them consistently.

fields.desc: Identifies the tributary port for the assigned slot or slots.

fields.name: Length
fields.desc: Number of tributary-slot bits in the following bit map.
